newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Brazil-led group sues over Argentine post decision.
newsitem.headline: Brazil-led group sues over Argentine post decision.

text.p: A Brazilian-led group on Thursday said it has raised a court challenge to its disqualification from bidding for the 30-year concession to run Argentina's state-run postal company, ENCOTESA.
"We filed yesterday a lawsuit asking to continue in the process," Jose Chalen, representative of the group headed by Brazilian airline VASP, told Reuters.
On Tuesday, the group presented a related complaint to Cabinet chief Jorge Rodriguez, he said.

The commission in charge of ENCOTESA's privatization last month rejected appeals from the Brazilian-led group and two others that were disqualified. The three challengers had to deposit $500,000, which ENCOTESA said they would lose because their appeals to the commission failed.

The commission said the Brazilian-led group failed to present a complete investment plan as required. On Thursday, Chalen said the group went to court because the investment plan was included in the body of their presentation.

The group is composed of VASP with 60 percent, Argentina's Brazal with 20 percent, Argentina's Banco del Chubut with 10 percent and Argentine postal company Andreani with 10 percent. It had proposed Italy's post office as operator.
Chalen said the suit only seeks a reversal of the group's disqualification, not a halt of the privatization process.

The two other groups -- one led by ING Bank NV-Cayman Islands Funds NV and the other by Benito Roggio e Hijos SA, an Argentine construction company-- were disqualified on the grounds that they did not have the backing of official post offices, as required.
ING linked up with Nepostel Consultancy NV as postal operator, while Roggio took Canada Post System Management Ltd (CPSM). ENCOTESA said the two were consultants, not official postal operators.
ING and Roggio have said they are considering a court challenge to their disqualification but so far have made no announcements.
Conditions for ENCOTESA's concession include a $250 million investment plan over the first 10 years and then an additional annual investment of one percent over revenue.
Three other consortia have qualified to bid for the concession:
-- Local transport company TAC, local group Roman and businessman Samuel Liberman, owner of local cable TV firm VCC, with Germany's state post office as operator.
-- Itron and Sideco --controlled by local holding company Grupo Macri-- and local Banco de Galicia, with the British Post Office.
-- Local banking group Werthein and COINTEL, a holding company that controls Telefonica de Argentina, and New Zealand's Infratil International with New Zealand Post.
COINTEL is owned by Telefonica de Espana, operator of Telefonica de Argentina, and Argentina's CEI Citicorp Holding SA, which is about 40 percent indirectly owned by Citicorp.
